html:
Rafael Ángel Calderón Guardia was a Costa Rican doctor who, as president from 1940 to 1944, brought in the country's social security system, its labour code and its national university.

A Catholic inspired by the social teaching of the Church, he founded the University of Costa Rica in 1940 and the Social Security Fund in 1941. In 1943 he added social guarantees to the constitution and a labour code. To pass them he allied with the Church and the communists, which alarmed the coffee elite.

His party's attempt to keep power by annulling the election of 1948 set off the civil war, and he went into exile. Yet the winners under José Figueres kept his reforms. He is honoured as a builder of the welfare state of Costa Rica, alongside the end of the army.
sum: Rafael Ángel Calderón Guardia was a Costa Rican doctor who, as president from 1940 to 1944, brought in the country's social security system, its labour code and its national university.
